questions.text: A man bought a cycle for ₹1,400 and sold it for ₹1,120. Find the loss percentage.
questions.hint1: Loss = CP − SP. Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100

questions.text: The ratio of ages of A and B is 5:7. If B is 35 years old, what is A's age?
questions.hint1: If the ratio is 5:7 and B = 35, find the value of one part.
questions.explanation: One part = 35/7 = 5. A's age = 5 × 5 = 25 years. Answer: B

questions.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours. Another pipe can empty it in 18 hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.hint1: Net rate = Fill rate − Empty rate per hour.
questions.explanation: Fill rate = 1/12, Empty rate = 1/18. Net rate = 1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36. Time to fill = 36 hours. Answer: B

questions.text: The simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years is:
If the perimeter of a square is 48 cm, what is its area?
questions.hint1: Perimeter of square = 4 × side. Find side first.
questions.hint2: Side = 48/4 = 12 cm. Area = side².
questions.explanation: Side = 48/4 = 12 cm. Area = 12² = 144 cm². Answer: A

questions.text: Two trains are running in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 90 km/h. Their lengths are 120 m and 180 m. How long will they take to cross each other?
questions.hint1: Relative speed = sum of speeds (opposite direction). Convert km/h to m/s.
questions.hint2: Relative speed = 150 km/h = 150 × 5/18 m/s. Total distance = 120 + 180 m.
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 150 km/h = 125/3 m/s. Distance = 300 m. Time = 300/(125/3) = 7.2 seconds. Answer: B

questions.text: If tan θ = 4/3, what is the value of sec θ?
questions.hint1: sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ

questions.text: If x² − 5x + 6 = 0, find the values of x.
questions.hint1: Factorise the quadratic: find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to −5.
questions.explanation: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. So x = 2, 3. Answer: B

questions.text: A sum of money doubles in 5 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest?
questions.hint1: If money doubles, SI = Principal. Use SI = PRT/100.
questions.explanation: SI = P (doubles). P = P × R × 5/100. R = 100/5 = 20%. Answer: B

questions.text: The average of first 50 natural numbers is:
questions.hint1: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2.

questions.text: Find the missing number in the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
questions.hint1: Find the differences between consecutive terms.
questions.hint2: Differences: 5, 7, 9, 11, ? — increasing by 2 each time.
questions.explanation: Differences: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. So 35 + 13 = 48. Answer: B

questions.text: If MONEY is coded as PRQHB, then HONEY is coded as:
questions.hint1: Compare each letter: M→P (+3), O→R (+3), N→Q (+3)...
questions.hint2: Each letter is shifted +3 positions. Apply this to HONEY: H→K, O→R, N→Q, E→H, Y→B.
questions.explanation: Each letter +3: H→K, O→R, N→Q, E→H, Y→B. HONEY = KRQHB. Answer: A

questions.text: A is the brother of B. C is the mother of A. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.hint1: C is A's mother. D is C's father.
questions.hint2: So D is the father of A's mother = A's maternal grandfather.
questions.explanation: D is A's mother's father, so A is D's grandson. Answer: B

questions.text: If South-East becomes North, then North-East becomes:
questions.hint1: South-East is rotated 135° clockwise to become North. Apply same rotation.
questions.hint2: Rotating all directions clockwise by 135°: North-East → West.
questions.explanation: If SE → N (135° clockwise rotation), then NE → W. Answer: B

questions.text: Select the Venn diagram that best represents: Dogs, Animals, Cats
options: Two separate circles inside a larger circle
Two overlapping circles inside a larger circle
questions.hint1: Dogs and Cats are both types of Animals.
questions.hint2: Dogs and Cats are separate groups, both inside Animals.
questions.explanation: Dogs and Cats are distinct subsets of Animals — two separate circles inside a larger circle. Answer: A

questions.text: Which number replaces the question mark? 7 : 50 :: 11 : ?
questions.hint1: Find the relationship: 7² + 1 = 50.

questions.text: Arrange in meaningful order: 1) Diagnosis 2) Doctor 3) Treatment 4) Patient 5) Recovery
questions.hint1: Start from the first logical step in a medical process.
questions.hint2: Patient goes to Doctor → Doctor makes Diagnosis → Treatment → Recovery.
questions.explanation: Patient(4) → Doctor(2) → Diagnosis(1) → Treatment(3) → Recovery(5). Answer: A

questions.text: Choose the odd one out: 17, 23, 29, 33, 37
questions.hint1: Check which numbers are prime.
questions.hint2: 17, 23, 29, 37 are all prime numbers. 33 = 3 × 11.
questions.explanation: 33 is not a prime number (33 = 3 × 11). All others are prime. Answer: C

questions.text: A cube has how many edges?
questions.hint1: A cube has 6 faces, 8 vertices, and how many edges?
questions.hint2: Each face has 4 edges, but each edge is shared by 2 faces: (6 × 4)/2
questions.explanation: A cube has 12 edges. (6 × 4)/2 = 12. Answer: C

questions.text: If Tuesday falls on the 4th of a month, what day will the 26th be?
questions.hint1: Find the number of days between 4th and 26th.
questions.hint2: 26 − 4 = 22 days. 22 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks + 1 day. Tuesday + 1 = ?
questions.explanation: 22 days difference = 3 weeks + 1 day. Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday. Answer: C

questions.text: Choose the synonym of 'ABATE':
questions.hint1: Abate relates to making something less intense.
questions.hint2: Think of reducing or diminishing something.
questions.explanation: 'Abate' means to become less intense, to reduce. Answer: B

questions.text: Spot the error: 'He (A) told to me (B) that he would (C) come tomorrow. (D) No error'
questions.hint1: 'Tell' is used differently than 'say' in English grammar.
questions.hint2: We say 'told me' not 'told to me'. Remove 'to'.
questions.explanation: 'Told to me' should be 'told me'. 'Tell' takes a direct object. Answer: B

questions.text: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'A penny for your thoughts'
questions.hint1: This idiom is used when asking someone who seems lost in thought.
questions.hint2: It's a way to ask someone to share their thoughts.
questions.explanation: 'A penny for your thoughts' is used to ask what someone is thinking about. Answer: B

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Neither the teacher ___ the students were present.'
questions.hint1: 'Neither' is always paired with a specific conjunction.
questions.hint2: The correct pair is 'Neither...nor'.
questions.explanation: 'Neither...nor' is the correct correlative conjunction pair. Answer: B

questions.text: Choose the one-word substitution for: 'A government ruled by the people'
questions.hint1: 'Demo' relates to people in Greek.
questions.hint2: Demo + cracy = rule of the people.
questions.explanation: Democracy = government by the people (demos = people, kratos = rule). Answer: B

questions.text: Change to passive voice: 'The police arrested the thief.'
options: The thief is arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.
The thief has been arrested by the police.
The thief were arrested by the police.
questions.hint1: Original is in simple past tense. Use: Object + was/were + past participle + by + Subject.
questions.hint2: The thief + was + arrested + by + the police.
questions.explanation: 'The thief was arrested by the police.' Simple past passive. Answer: B

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelled word:
questions.hint1: The word has double 'c' and double 'r'.
questions.hint2: O-C-C-U-R-R-E-N-C-E
questions.explanation: Correct spelling: Occurrence (double c, double r). Answer: B

questions.text: Improve the sentence: 'He is more cleverer than his brother.'
questions.hint1: Using 'more' and '-er' together is a common grammatical error.
questions.hint2: Either use 'more clever' or 'cleverer', not both.
questions.explanation: 'More cleverer' is a double comparative. Correct: 'cleverer'. Answer: B

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'OPAQUE':
questions.hint1: Opaque means not allowing light to pass through.
questions.hint2: The opposite would mean allowing light to pass through clearly.
questions.explanation: Opaque (not see-through) ↔ Transparent (see-through). Answer: B

questions.text: Change to indirect speech: 'He said, "I have finished my work."'
options: He said that he has finished his work.
He said that he had finished his work.
He said that he have finished his work.
He told that he had finished his work.
questions.hint1: Change pronouns and apply back-shift of tense.
questions.hint2: 'Have finished' → 'had finished' in indirect speech.
questions.explanation: He said that he had finished his work. Present perfect → past perfect. Answer: B

questions.text: Who founded the Arya Samaj?
questions.hint1: He was a Hindu reformer from Gujarat.
questions.hint2: He wrote the book 'Satyarth Prakash'.
questions.explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875. Answer: B

questions.text: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the distribution of powers between Centre and States?
questions.hint1: It contains Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
questions.hint2: This schedule number is associated with three legislative lists.
questions.explanation: 7th Schedule contains three lists: Union, State, Concurrent. Answer: C

questions.text: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
questions.hint1: This river is known for frequent devastating floods in Bengal.
questions.hint2: It originates from the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
questions.explanation: Damodar River is called the 'Sorrow of Bengal' due to its frequent floods. Answer: B

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of Baking Soda?
questions.hint1: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate.
questions.hint2: It's sodium (Na) + hydrogen carbonate.
questions.explanation: Baking Soda = Sodium Bicarbonate = NaHCO₃. Answer: B

questions.text: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces?
questions.hint1: This person is the constitutional head of the state.
questions.hint2: Article 53 vests the executive power in this person.
questions.explanation: The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces. Answer: B

questions.text: The Quit India Movement was launched in which year?
questions.hint1: Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during this movement.
questions.hint2: It was during World War II, in the early 1940s.
questions.explanation: Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 by Mahatma Gandhi. Answer: C

questions.text: Which mineral is known as 'Black Gold'?
questions.hint1: It's a combustible sedimentary rock used as fuel.
questions.hint2: It is black in color and extremely valuable as an energy resource.
questions.explanation: Coal is known as 'Black Gold' due to its immense value. Answer: C

questions.text: The phenomenon of 'Mirage' is due to:
questions.hint1: Light rays bend when passing through layers of air at different temperatures.
questions.hint2: When light passes from denser to rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle.
questions.explanation: Mirage is caused by total internal reflection of light in layers of hot air. Answer: C

questions.text: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.hint1: It plays a role in digestion, detoxification, and protein synthesis.
questions.hint2: It is located in the upper right part of the abdomen.
questions.explanation: The Liver is the largest gland in the human body. Answer: C

questions.text: Which Five Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis Model?
questions.hint1: It focused on rapid industrialization with heavy industries.
questions.hint2: It was implemented from 1956 to 1961.
questions.explanation: Second Five Year Plan (1956–61) was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis Model. Answer: B
